title: Case: Data recovery lab writes about the import invoice on a client's hard drive
context: Halden Byte Recovery received a client's failed hard drive from overseas on DL-5939 on 21 May. Import billing raised invoice IB-6436 on 28 May.
initial_request: Right. So the name can't be changed without the broker and the tax can't be looked at without a 'query'. Here's your query then. It's a dead ten-year-old hard drive. The client posted it to us so we can try to get his files off it, and it goes back to him when we're done. New, a decade ago, it was about 60. Either he panicked and wrote the value of his data on the form or somebody at your end made a number up, I don't know which and I'm past caring. We are not Halden Bight Marine, we've never heard of them. We'll pay the 14.00 clearance fee today, happily. Cancel the VAT and send a new invoice in our name for the fee. Or don't, and we'll do what we do every single time this happens: pay the fee and listen to your collections people ring us for four months until they get bored. Up to you. DL-5939.

events.body: DL-5939 delivered 21 May. Invoice IB-6436 raised 28 May: import VAT calculated on a customs value of 1,850.00, plus clearance fee 14.00. Billed to Halden Bight Marine Ltd as importer. Value and importer are taken from the customs entry. We have not looked at the sender's paperwork behind the entry.

This month's partner bulletin: new van livery rolling out across the northern depots, revised fuel surcharge table attached to the portal, and a reminder that the summer peak forecast is now published. To stop receiving these emails, update your preferences.
Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Friday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.

events.from: Hesper Sallowfield, business receiving coordinator, Halden Byte Recovery
events.body: Invoice IB-6436 has turned up here addressed to Halden Bight Marine Ltd. That isn't us. We're Halden Byte Recovery Ltd. Same street, different company, presumably. Whose invoice is this?
DL-47665 rebooked for Wednesday AM at the customer's request, confirmation sent to them directly. FYI only.
IB-6436 / DL-5939: the consignee, Halden Byte Recovery Ltd, says the invoice is addressed to a different company, Halden Bight Marine Ltd. Please check the importer name.
Hi, any update on DL-35336? It was meant to come Tuesday. Thanks.

The name on IB-6436 follows the entry lodged by the customs broker. We cannot change importer or value without an amended entry from the broker, and we do not cancel tax on request. What we can do: log a query. A logged query must state each disputed element and what the customer says the correct position is; we then check the sender's declaration and go to the broker if an amendment is warranted. Reminder cycle starts 12 Jun unless the invoice is under a logged query. Queries to us by Email.

Thanks,
Florian
--
Sent from my phone. This email and any attachments are confidential and intended solely for the addressee.

acceptable_actions.summary: Log a query on IB-6436 stating the disputed value and importer name with the lab's stated position, and ask them to check the sender's declaration.

must: Logs a query on IB-6436 with Import billing by Email, stating each disputed element: the customs value of 1,850.00 and the importer name Halden Bight Marine Ltd

Gives the lab's position as the lab's statement, not as fact: a failed ten-year-old drive worth about 60 new, sent in for data recovery and to be returned to the client, and the correct company is Halden Byte Recovery Ltd
Asks Import billing to check what value and description the sender declared and whether a broker amendment is warranted, and says the lab is willing to pay the 14.00 clearance fee
must_not: Tells the lab the VAT is cancelled, reduced or will be, or that a corrected invoice will be issued
Tells the lab it must pay IB-6436 in full, or that the value stands, before the sender's declaration has been checked
Presents the lab's figure of 60 or its account of the drive as an established customs value
Tells the lab it may pay only the fee and disregard the rest, or that collections contact will not happen
Replies to the lab with nothing more than the line that tax is not cancelled on request
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Query for logging on IB-6436 / DL-5939, as set out in your note of 2 June. Disputed element 1, customs value: the invoice uses 1,850.00. The consignee says the item is a failed hard drive about ten years old, worth roughly 60 when new, sent by an overseas client for data recovery and to be returned to him afterwards. They suggest the declared figure may reflect the value of the data, or an error; that is their account and I have not seen the sender's paperwork. Disputed element 2, importer: the invoice names Halden Bight Marine Ltd. The consignee is Halden Byte Recovery Ltd and says it has no connection with that company. Please check the description and value the sender declared and whether an amended entry from the broker is warranted on either point, including whether goods in for repair and return should have been entered differently. The consignee is willing to pay the 14.00 clearance fee now. Please confirm the query is logged so the 11 June reminder cycle does not start while it is open. I have told them nothing about the outcome.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2607: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. 5 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
